statements.text: Vermonters deserve to know that when they are looking at a campaign ad, that it's actually the person it claims to be, and that's why we need stronger AI regulation now, not later.

Artists, creators, and anyone who uses the internet must have the basic right to control digital replicas of their own voice and image. AI is moving fast, and we need to make sure these guardrails are in place now, not later. The NO FAKES Act is a commonsense, bipartisan, and essential bill.
statements.venue: Press release on NO FAKES Act reintroduction

statements.text: Specifically, I would like your thoughts on generative AI and competition. It is tough to imagine online platforms gaining even more power, but it seems that Big Tech firms who control their own AI systems and access to cloud data are in a position to do just that. I find that alarming, as do many of my constituents back in Vermont. So, what I would like to ask you is how could AI technology lead to an even more consolidated internet landscape with even few choices for consumers?
statements.context: House oversight hearing with FTC Chair Khan, during a line of questioning on AI and competition.

statements.text: Congress has to rise above partisanship to create guardrails around AI that addresses risk and supports safe innovation. This rapidly changing technology and industry requires our attention to get it right. https://t.co/XFPZKOIEo7

We can be careful in our regulations. We can be careful in the guardrails that we're putting on, but I don't think anyone here, at least I hope not, that anyone on the Antitrust Committee would be supportive of landlords colluding to raise the price of rent, and I know in some instances, we've seen that this AI dynamic pricing scheme has led to increases of over $800 over the course of a year of not just these hidden fees that we're talking about, but the prices that they're paying for rent itself.
statements.context: Senate Judiciary subcommittee hearing on AI innovation and competition, where the speaker raises concrete consumer and labor harms from AI deployment and defends FTC oversight.

statements.text: It's so important that we don't lose sight of the central point here, which is how does this technology help or hurt working people?
statements.context: House hearing titled 'Artificial Intelligence: Examining Trends in Innovation and Competition,' where Rep. Balint questions FTC commissioners.

statements.text:
The Pentagon has signed a $200 million agreement to use Grok, Elon Musk's AI chatbot, according to xAI.

Despite the social media wars, the Trump-Elon corruption machine is alive and well.
Yet, here we are, first hearing back. We're not talking about the AI platforms that are leading kids to self-harm. We're not talking about the algorithms profiting off teens' eating disorders.
statements.context: Rep. Balint delivers opening remarks at a hearing examining Europe's regulatory approach to American tech companies and speech.

statements.text:
Let me get this straight: in order to see if your medical procedure is covered by insurance, the government will use AI to decide if it is really necessary??

For-profit companies will deny care for seniors and working people to get richer. Despicable. https://t.co/AY7Lxgex6O
Americans deserve affordable, quality healthcare, and AI should not be determining whether you get healthcare. [...] That is what Democrats are fighting for.
statements.context: Floor speech by Rep. Becca Balint on healthcare affordability, criticizing a CMS proposal to use AI in medical-necessity determinations.

statements.text: I feel like there’s going to be a bunch of work that happens around intellectual property, around AI, and holding big tech accountable.

Artists, creators, and anyone on the internet must have the basic right to control digital replicas of their own voice and image. Given how fast AI is moving, we need protections in place now.

I'm proud to be leading the NO FAKES Act to get this done.
https://t.co/6JTpi5LtUt

A political opponent recently posted a deepfake video of me on social media. It was generated using AI and fabricated my voice and image to put words in my mouth. While it represents a new - and dangerous - low, it was not unpredictable.

It just drives home why we need to act now to give people protections against unauthorized AI replicas of their name and likeness. Let’s start by passing my NO FAKES Act.

I'm concerned about this not just for me but for anyone in elected office who wants Vermonters to hear directly from them. [...] Right now, anyone can make an AI-generated clip of them, post it online, and have absolutely no protections really.

It is AI slop. There's a lot of it. We're going to see, unfortunately, more of it because we have not, at the federal level, put any guardrails on this and we need to. Vermonters should know that when they see a picture of me, when they hear my voice, when they see me speaking, that it's actually me.

More broadly, look, AI needs guard rails. And I think a lot of Americans don't understand that right now as it exists you don't have a private right of action for your image, for your voice, for these AI deep fakes. And so I have introduced the No Fakes Act.

Young people are using AI chatbots every day. We need clear rules, research, and accountability for Big Tech companies developing them to make sure they don’t put their profits ahead of the well-being of our kids.
 
I'm proud to be introducing the Addictive Design Act so we can take action before it's too late.

This weekend, Trump posted an AI-generated image of himself trading stocks in the Oval Office. This comes as he’s sending our servicemembers into war and Americans can’t afford their daily lives.

He doesn’t know the first thing about loyalty to the American people. https://t.co/NgCoXn2YPc

The time for burying our heads in the sand is over. If the people working directly on these technologies are saying this, it’s time to pump the brakes.

We can’t let these massive AI companies literally gamble with the future of humanity. https://t.co/O6lGmg793U
statements.quoted: Jacob is correct here—we really do earnestly believe AI could kill all humans! I personally think it is >10% within the next decade. I believe Anthropic is trying its best, but we do not yet have a plan to solve alignment for superintelligence and are not clearly on track to. https://t.co/QAIHiFP3QZ

statements.text:
Congress must urgently hold hearings on frontier research. The leaders of these massive AI companies owe us transparency about what they're doing.

We can’t afford to continue the Trump strategy of letting billionaires play with the safety of humanity. https://t.co/XFecgr1b2Z

So the AI companies want to be the ones to set the rules and Trump thinks that he’s the only person capable of setting the rules…

What they’re all saying is that Congress and the American people shouldn’t have a role. It’s an absolute insult to everyone who’s raising genuine concerns right now.

Where do we even begin with this?

It may be barely coherent, but it’s damn scary that Trump is gaslighting us about our genuine concerns about AI and that he is also clearly only interested in how much profit these technologies will make his billionaire friends. https://t.co/JpugrwpuQn
statements.quoted: Trump: "Concerning AI, when, in the History of Business, did anyone see the Leaders of an Industry call for Regulation that, if strongly implemented, will drive them into oblivion and bankruptcy? AI taking over the World, destroying Humanity, and all other things bad, is a HOAX, no different from RUSSIA, RUSSIA, RUSSIA — UKRAINE, UKRAINE, UKRAINE — IMPEACHMENT HOAX #1 — IMPEACHMENT HOAX #2 — and all of the other HOAXES and SCAMS that America was forced to endure through the Destructionists’ and Deviants’ foul play and illegal conduct. President Xi, of China, just announced that China will be doing absolutely nothing to stand in the way of AI, or its future. Google has recently stated that they want to build a massive Plant in Finland, all because they are finding permitting too difficult in the United States. I am not happy about this, and want them to change their thinking. AI, and Data Centers, will be the Greatest Economic Development Engine in History ­­— Bigger than Oil, Gold, Diamonds, or even the Internet. It will not be stopped by brilliantly run Destructive Forces during the Term of President DONALD J. TRUMP!"

statements.text:
Let’s be very clear about what’s happening here: the AI companies have had this “change of heart” because they want to be the ones to write the rules about how they’re regulated.
 
We can’t just sit on our hands and trust them to police themselves. https://t.co/FAK1XIaTaM

Yes! There’s something special about the human experience of creating new art – and about consuming art made by fellow humans.
 
This is why my colleagues and I introduced the NO FAKES Act. Artists need protections against unauthorized AI replicas of their voice and likeness. https://t.co/Ne7DgfZJ5H
statements.quoted: In this era of artificial intelligence, it is becoming urgent to distinguish human art from what machines produce. There is an ontological difference, even before an aesthetic one, between art and what a machine can generate through statistical calculation based on millions of images created by others. Algorithms lack the spark of humanity. For this reason, the Church wishes to renew an alliance with artists and cultural institutions to safeguard our humanity.

statements.text:
Despite what Trump and these tech CEOs said this week, Americans want guardrails on AI - not for the companies to police themselves.

This issue has major implications in communities all over the country. We’ve got to get this right. https://t.co/A0nbYHNHQ0

Clearly, these AI systems are faulty or broken products. We already have laws on the books to protect us from stuff like this.

It’s only a question of whether or not we’re willing to enforce them. https://t.co/BWD8Y8NpD3

There’s a business in Vermont that is laying off 60 people because of its investment in AI. Those jobs are going to AI agents, and I do worry about the economic future that you face and also my own kids.
statements.venue: UVM student town hall, reported by Vermont Cynic

statements.text: We are concerned that McDonald’s may be using AI to squeeze consumers into paying higher prices, and that its AI pricing tools may facilitate collusion between franchisees who should be operating as competitors.
statements.venue: Joint letter with Sen. Warren and colleagues to McDonald's CEO (press release)

Big Tech needs to stop forcing AI on us - in schools and otherwise. https://t.co/ilrX4Z8Clm

statements.text:
We’re not lovin’ this… 
 
Folks are already paying too much for food. The last thing they need is a massive company like McDonald’s using AI to raise prices and facilitate collusion among their franchisees. 
 
We’re demanding answers on behalf of our constituents. https://t.co/bKNBsyr3bL

Voters in Vermont and across the country are demanding we push back on the AI industry's unchecked power.
 
We'd be foolish to let them off the hook. https://t.co/fGIbxllt23

Technology companies have spent years learning how to capture our attention and keep us engaged for as long as possible. They should not be allowed to apply those same tactics to vulnerable kids who may be turning to an AI chatbot during a mental health crisis, [...] As a parent to two teenagers, I have already seen the devastating consequences of a tech and social media industry that puts engagement and profit ahead of people’s well-being. We can't make the same mistake with AI. We need clear rules, research, and accountability before more families are forced to suffer the consequences.
